page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hpc8i.32xlarge is a high-performance computing instance powered by Intel Xeon 8575C processors on the x86_64 architecture. Virtualized using the KVM hypervisor, this instance provides 64 dedicated vCPUs operating at a nominal clock frequency of 2.8 GHz. It is equipped with 512 GB of system memory, establishing a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per vCPU. Networking throughput is defined by a baseline bandwidth of 100 Gbps, facilitating high-speed data transfer across distributed nodes without bundled complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

From an infrastructure and storage perspective, the ecs.hpc8i.32xlarge provides no onboard local disk storage and contains no discrete GPU accelerators. Operating diskless requires relying on remote cloud storage architectures for persistent system volumes and operating scratch spaces. The 100 Gbps network capacity helps offset the absence of direct-attached drives by maintaining high-bandwidth interfaces to external network storage fabrics and adjacent cluster components.

Cost efficiency aligns with high-density enterprise infrastructure where dedicated core allocation and substantial memory capacity minimize resource contention. The 1:8 compute-to-memory configuration avoids underutilizing execution threads during memory-heavy tasks. This technical profile makes the instance suitable for distributed high-performance computing workloads, memory-intensive computational fluid dynamics, large-scale scientific modeling, cluster-based ETL data transformations, and distributed caching environments.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hpc8i.32xlarge is a dedicated high-performance computing instance built on the x86_64 architecture using the KVM hypervisor. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8575C processor running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz, the instance delivers 64 dedicated vCPUs alongside 512 GB of system memory, maintaining an 8 GB per vCPU memory allocation ratio. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage or onboard GPU acceleration, requiring network-attached block storage solutions for persistent data needs. With a baseline network bandwidth interface of 100 Gbps and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, it is engineered for tight inter-node communications across high-throughput clusters. The combination of dense dedicated processing cores, substantial memory capacity, and high-speed networking makes the instance appropriate for compute-intensive and memory-demanding enterprise tasks, including parallel high-performance scientific simulations, large in-memory data processing, distributed compilation jobs, and financial modeling.
